build: Rust stable release --locked --offline, separate initially empty CARGO_TARGET_DIR per revision; benchmark adapter copied unchanged into old source

machine.filesystem_backing: Unknown; overlay physical storage is not independently verified.

limitations: Closed-loop, cached byte-key workloads; no offered-load control, coordinated omission correction, SQL query or transaction benchmark, multi-project isolation, large datasets, independent power-loss validation, or universal ranking.

All clients use TCP loopback. Prototype and SQLite run behind a purpose-built native adapter; PostgreSQL and Redis use their own protocols and Docker port forwarding. Python driver and network overhead differ, as do feature sets.

Prototype syncs log and commit witness before acknowledgement; SQLite WAL synchronous FULL, PostgreSQL fsync/synchronous_commit/full_page_writes on, Redis AOF appendfsync always. These are not identical complete durability guarantees.
Redis is memory-resident and stores four extra checksum bytes in each value; prototype/SQLite/PostgreSQL use distinct internal checksum/storage formats.
Runs are short on a shared virtualized CPU and filesystem; p99.9 has few samples. Report run ranges and do not infer stable differences from overlapping noisy results.
